title: Vectors in CockroachDB
text: CockroachDB stores embeddings in a VECTOR column alongside relational data, so the vector and the record it describes are written in the same transaction. There is no separate vector store to keep in sync, and a search can join embeddings back to the business data in one query.

title: Vector Indexing
text: A vector index in CockroachDB uses approximate nearest-neighbor search over partitions built with k-means clustering. It is generally available in v26.2 and enabled with the feature.vector_index.enabled cluster setting. The index accelerates the cosine-distance operator used by semantic search.

title: The CockroachDB Operator
text: On Kubernetes, CockroachDB is deployed by the GA CockroachDB Operator using CrdbCluster and CrdbNode custom resources. There are no StatefulSets. The operator treats every node as an independent, replaceable resource, so it can replace any node freely and reuse its disk without the ordering constraints a StatefulSet imposes.

title: Resilience and Consensus
text: CockroachDB replicates every range across multiple nodes and commits writes by majority consensus using the Raft protocol. When a single node goes down, a majority of replicas still hold every committed write, so no committed data is lost and the surviving replicas keep serving reads and writes. The cluster automatically up-replicates to restore the desired replication factor once a node is gone.

title: Stateless RAG Application
text: The RAG application is a stateless FastAPI service. All durable state lives in CockroachDB, which lets Kubernetes scale, kill, and reschedule the app pods freely without data loss. Any replica can serve any request because nothing is cached on the pod's local disk.

title: Autoscaling the Platform
text: The Horizontal Pod Autoscaler adds and removes replicas based on demand. The lab's chart scales on CPU because embedding is CPU work, which metrics-server can measure out of the box. In production a RAG request is often latency-bound waiting on an LLM, so CPU can look idle under load; the recommended pattern is to scale on a custom metric such as requests per second per pod.

title: Liveness vs Readiness
text: A liveness probe asks whether the process is alive; failing it restarts the container. A readiness probe asks whether the pod can serve traffic; failing it removes the pod from the Service without restarting it. A lost database connection should make the app not ready, not dead, so a database blip never triggers a restart storm.

title: Transaction Retries
text: Because CockroachDB offers serializable isolation, under contention it may return a retry error with SQLSTATE 40001. This is expected behavior, not a failure; application code should wrap transactions in a retry loop with backoff rather than surfacing these errors to users.
